steps.content: [Bureau Corridor]
A shrill alarm blares throughout the Bureau. The corridor, once neat and orderly, lies now in shambles.
Papers scatter through the air; cups topple over. In the next instant, a dark tide erupts from every vent, pipe crack, and the edges of electronic access panels.

Centipedes mingle with pillbugs; spiders weave their threads among snakes. They blanket the floors and walls with alarming speed, encasing the modern facilities beneath a writhing, glistening layer of living matter.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief! Big problem! We're picking up major biosigns. There's gotta be... dozens? No, hundreds of bugs and snakes are flooding the whole building!

Wynn clutches a terminal to her chest and nearly collides with you as you step out of your office. She anxiously raises the device, its screen swarms with a dense cluster of red dots scattered throughout every corner of the Bureau. One area shows an especially concentrated mass.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Looks like it's all coming from... the Outdoor Activity Area!

You rush to the Outdoor Activity Area. As expected, the insect swarm has already overrun it, a writhing shadow given form. Within that darkness, an unusual Mania fluctuation makes itself known to you.

The crescent moon hangs high, insect shadows run deep; some rejoice while others despair! This granny just came for a peek, not to tear the place down. Must everyone get their britches in such a twist?

The humming pauses, then a charming, playful voice rises from deep within the swarm. As if commanded, the venomous insects and serpents part to either side, revealing the mastermind hidden among them—
Well, well. Such a grand place you've got here, <color=#fb9259>little one</color>.
The girl speaks in a light, casual tone, as if she were your acquaintance. But those grayish-white eyes hold you like a hunter watching prey, rippling with unmistakable satisfaction.
[Chief's Office]

A Few Days Later
Chief's Office

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The vermin inside the Bureau have been largely eradicated. One logistics staff member sustained a minor head injury after being startled by a flying cockroach and striking a desk corner. No other casualties or property damage have been logged.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The Sinner responsible for the disturbance has been identified as <color=#fb9259>Ayiguo</color>. She expressed a voluntary desire to remain in Bureau custody and is currently detained pending standard medical clearance.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: However, she has declined to communicate with any staff besides you, Chief. In the past 72 hours, we have received 17 informal complaints regarding her conduct. I strongly advise scheduling her interrogation at the earliest opportunity.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Seventeen complaints already? What's she been doing that even you're in a hurry to get her interrogated?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Her infractions include, but are not limited to: adulterating the cafeteria soup stock with an unknown insect-and-herb mixture she described as an "Eastian delicacy." She also presented live beetles to EMP, whose subsequent reaction caused a short in an electrical panel and a 34-minute localized power disruption. Additionally, she employed some method to temporarily neutralize the sense of taste in several staff members who glanced in her direction.
As Nightingale lists out the incidents caused by this mysterious Eastian visitor at the Bureau one by one, a headache is already building behind your eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She's from Eastia, and she seems to know me. But I don't remember meeting anyone like her at Northsnow Manor...
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Granny</color>...
[Flashback]
No, wait. There is someone. Your hazy memory holds an encounter with a mysterious girl, though you cannot say whether it belongs to a dream or to reality.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Her demonstrated capabilities and potential threat level significantly exceed our expectations. Additionally, her <color=#fb9259>physiology</color> presents several anomalies. The medical report contains multiple unidentifiable biomarkers, and toxic residue has been detected on both her epidermis and clothing.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I must urge you to maintain extreme vigilance during your interactions, Chief.

Your gaze lands on a screenshot from Ayiguo's apprehension a few days ago. Her seemingly innocent smile as she looks back from the center of the insect swarm merges with the playful expression in her profile photo.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yeah. I'll be careful. Whatever she can do, and whatever she's really here for... I'll get to the bottom of it.
Ayiguo sits cross-legged, her wrist rotating idly as she watches a small spider trace futile circles around it.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: My, my... you're a tough one to pin down for a chat, little one. Is this the Disian way to treat a weary guest who's traveled from afar?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Guests usually knock before they swarm the door. We're not used to this kind of entrance.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Oh, don't be such a stick in the mud! A proper visit requires a proper gift. Everyone knows that.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Those little darlings were my welcoming party for you. And judging by all that delightful hollering, I'd say my gift was quite the hit.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Can't say I'm up to speed on Eastian party etiquette. So, vermin control is your thing? And you still haven't told me how you tracked this location.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Those fellows are just a bit of roadside riffraff I picked up along the way. A little flash to let you know I was coming.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: This is proper control.
With a curl of her fingertip, a small spider—silver-white with cyan-tinged legs—emerges from beneath your collar. No sooner does it touch the ground than it scurries toward her.
The spider on her wrist cedes its spot without hesitation. They swap places in one fluid motion, and the newcomer nestles affectionately against Ayiguo's finger.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: There you are, my sweet little Seven. Did you have a nice ride? She hitched a lift all the way here, and I just followed the string between us.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: I must say, hiding away inside this giant tin can... how very dramatic. Took a fair bit of oomph just to find a crack in the door.
This creature was hiding on you as far back as Northsnow Manor? And you noticed nothing at all?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What were you doing at Northsnow Manor? I never saw your face among the guests.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Well, of course you didn't! No invitation, no grand entrance. I had to make do, so I slipped in through the back. Word of that legendary codex traveled fast, you know. Who wouldn't want to sneak a peek? I simply wanted to see it for myself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You trailed me all the way to DisCity, then stuck your neck out breaking into the Bureau. It's enough detours. What's the real reason?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: You've got them, don't you? Those... red, spiky things. Shackles, yes? That's what you call them?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Do you think a frail little thing like me would drag herself all the way to this strange land if she had any other road to walk?
Chin resting in her hand, her eyes soften suddenly as her voice assumes a deliberately fragile tone.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: When I was just a sprout, nasty folk snatched me up. Made me steep my bones in poison—day in, day out. I wriggled free eventually, but the damage was done. It's like a nest of hungry worms in here, always chewing, never quiet.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: At the manor, I felt it. Your shackles... they made the gnawing stop. So I thought... maybe you could lend a hand and heal me up proper.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're telling me I used the shackles on you back at Northsnow Manor? I'm drawing a blank on that.
Seeing that you cut straight to the heart of the matter, Ayiguo chooses to deflect instead.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Ahem. Well, you were in quite a fog then, dear. Can't blame you for forgetting.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: But that's water under the bridge! Now, even if you haven't a drop of pity for a poor, aching girl, you've still got a job to do, don't you, Chief?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Precisely! Here I am: a strange Sinner, suspicious origins, broke into your big metal house uninvited. Your job is to keep Sinners in check with those lovely shackles, isn't it? I'm presenting myself! Go on, then, do your worst!
At the mention of shackles, Ayiguo eagerly presses her palms together and offers them to you, as though she can barely contain her anticipation of restraint.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You seem plenty stable to me. There's no need to restrain you with shackles.
Stable is an understatement. She still has enough energy to play games and keep things hidden from you.
Seeing that you remain unmoved, Ayiguo releases a resigned sigh.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Must I spell it out for you? All this fuss is just a brave face. But fine, if you're going to be dense about it, the least you could do is stop jabbing at a girl's wounds.
You arch an eyebrow and wait to see where she takes this performance next.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Years and years, I've kept to myself, hidden away. All so no one else would get hurt. Day after day, night after night, just me and this gnawing ache, hoping for one clean breath. One ordinary day.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: As if the poison wasn't a curse enough, Mania had to sink its teeth in too. Now look at me. Not quite human, not quite ghost! Hideous marks all over. Can't even cover them properly.

Ayiguo's body does indeed carry many strangely colored markings. You have assumed until now that they are traditional Eastian patterns, yet it appears far more probable that they are manifestations of poison, or perhaps mutations wrought by Mania.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You say you want to hide them. Your wardrobe tells a different story.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Oh, my! Stereotypes, even all the way out here in DisCity? I expected better.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Is it so wrong for a girl to want pretty things? To stroll down a sunny street, take in the noise and the bustle, feel alive without something chewing at her insides?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: You understand, don't you? This wanting to just... be normal?
She gazes at you expectantly, eyes bright and sparkling. She truly looks the part of an innocent, naive little girl.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I understand wanting that. But you're still lying to me.

Ayiguo's sob story rings plausible at first, yet it remains only a surface-level facade. The spider tracking you since Northsnow Manor, the elaborate breach of the Bureau, her offhand manner toward experiences that ought to be traumatic—all of it confirms that Ayiguo is anything but the innocent girl she portrays.
You reach out, spread open the files Nightingale has prepared, and slide them toward her.
test
test
test
test
test
test

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Eastia's outside our jurisdiction. Info's thin, but not that thin. Over a hundred suspicious deaths with your fingerprints on them, with the oldest one dating back sixty years. Among them, twenty-seven confirmed mass poisonings.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When Eastia was tearing itself apart, people lived in fear of a poison master. Someone who looked like a girl, moved like a ghost, and killed on a whim. Commanded every venomous thing that crawled or slithered.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She always had golden spiders in her shadow, so they called her... <color=#fb9259>Granny Goldspider</color>.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You call this wanting to be normal?
Ayiguo leans back in her chair, crosses her legs, and clicks her tongue in impatience. A cold smile curves her lips.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Well, well. You have been thorough. Fancy that, I had no idea I'd kept myself so entertained all these years.

The shift is instantaneous, which only makes her earlier act seem more effortless. She clearly does not care what you make of her. If the deception holds, fine. If not, she keeps plenty of other tricks up her sleeve.

Anyone who stirs chaos through Eastia's martial world cannot possibly be good. She is either a murderer who tramples human life like dirt, or some ancient monster stripped of all feeling. Either way, extreme caution is necessary.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sixty-plus years, and you still look like a girl. Is it the Mania? The poison? Or is something else keeping that body of yours from aging a day?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Maybe I'm just built stubborn. All those toxins I've swallowed over the years pickled me from the inside out, perhaps?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Well now, isn't that handy? A poisonous old monster like me, wandering loose in your tidy little city. How terribly dangerous! Quick, slap those shackles on and lock me up. It's for everyone's good.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're pushing awfully hard for something most Sinners would rather die than accept. The shackles mean surveillance. Obedience. A leash around your neck. You understand exactly what you're signing away, so what are you planning to do with them?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're capricious. Life and death with you is a coin toss on a bad mood. What assurance do I have that the moment I put those shackles on, you won't turn DisCity into a sequel to every massacre in that file?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Enough prattling! This granny came to you with open hands, and you can't even muster a "thank you"? Must I show you exactly what I'm capable of before you learn some manners?!

She has not even finished speaking when a dense rustling erupts from the corners of the interrogation room. Swarms of tiny insects emerge, drawn by Ayiguo, and the air fills with their shrill, piercing buzz.
Purple-black mist radiates from Ayiguo in waves, steadily filling the room as it closes in on you. She is releasing poison on purpose! You quickly clamp a hand over your nose and mouth.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Still won't fight back? Fine! Let's see how long that stubborn body of yours holds out!

With Ayiguo's movements, the M-value in the interrogation room spikes sharply. Alarms blare, and red warning lights wash over everything. Something writhes and churns beneath her skin, inside her vessels, as if her veins carry not blood, but a tide of insects.

Window frames and door frames groan; even the steel-reinforced concrete strains under the pressure. If you hesitate any longer, the interrogation room will buckle under the force of the Mania, and poison will seep through every fissure into the world beyond. She is forcing your hand.
The shackles' crimson light tears through the poisonous fog, coiling straight for Ayiguo. Her body convulses hard as insects rain from the walls and ceiling in a pattering downpour.

She spits a mouthful of blood—purple-black gore alive with writhing things. Still, she laughs in triumph, utterly indifferent to the wretched sight she presents with blood pouring from her lips and nose.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Yes... there! It works! It really works!
You immediately withdraw the shackles.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Why did you stop?! Keep going! Now!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's enough. You caught me off guard once. I won't be maneuvered twice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll have Nightingale arrange maximum security, isolation, and full surveillance. Your movement will be restricted, and any access to me or the shackles will be cut off completely. Unless you're ready to tell me why you're really here. You want the shackles? Trade me the truth.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Questions, questions, questions! Good grief! You Disians are so complicated! Won't use them, won't stop using them, always have to poke and prod and interrogate everything!

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: I told you to use the shackles. So use them. Don't think for a second I won't poison you mute, hollow out that busy little mind of yours, and make you my puppet. Then you'll use them whenever I say!
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Granny</color>. Look at you, head full of cotton, can't remember your own name, probably. What's the point of explaining?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Don't bother with thanks. Granny just brushed some snow off. If you'd gone and kicked the bucket here, all my running around this godforsaken manor all day would've been for nothing!
[Flashback]
Your confrontation with Ayiguo stirs something deep inside. Hazy memories of Northsnow Manor sharpen and come clear.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's coming back now. You can't actually control people with your poison, can you? Otherwise, you would have done it back at the manor instead of playing tag with your insects all the way here.
You finish laying out your theory, and she falls abruptly silent. You have struck true.

The interrogation room lights flicker, mirroring Ayiguo's volatile mood. One moment she grits her teeth in apparent fury; the next, she shifts into languid indifference. The poison thins and dissipates, the insect swarm recedes, and she resumes her former appearance. She seems to be out of tricks. Unable to overpower you, she has little choice but to negotiate.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: You ungrateful little brat. Since you remember this granny saved your hide, shouldn't you be showing a bit of gratitude instead of all this suspicion?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: I wasn't sure about those shackles of yours before. Poked at them a few times but couldn't get them to bite. Coming here was a gamble, I'll admit. But now? Now I know they work beautifully. And what I told you before wasn't all lies.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Using them on me costs you nothing. You even get a dangerous granny on a leash. I fail to see the hesitation. For one so young, you're more tangled than a spider's web.
After that exchange, you are certain beyond any doubt that she truly came for the shackles, and her obsession with them runs deep.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Oh... is that it? You're afraid that if you use them on me, I'll flip the leash around and lead you? How does a coward like you manage a whole bureau of Sinners? Did you whimper and beg your way into that chair?

She props her feet up on the armrest and lets words tumble out unchecked, though her eyes stay vacant and far away as though she is savoring some private memory. Perhaps the shackles really do relieve her suffering, as she says, if only for that fleeting moment.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The shackles go both ways. I'm not taking that risk on a dare. You'll stay at the Bureau for now. Supervised, basic quarters. Until we have some actual trust to build on.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: During that time, if you try to move your swarms, release toxins, or threaten anyone, the arrangement ends. I'll contact the Eastian authorities and have you deported.
Ayiguo stares at you in silence, her eyes calm and cold as a spider's. She appears to weigh the odds of a successful cooperation.

Something skitters through the shadows, its scraping sounds deeply unsettling. Ayiguo's gaze sharpens into something vicious, though held in check. At last, it softens into stillness, and the world around her quiets in turn.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Well, well. A stubborn little stone, aren't you? It's been ages since anyone made this granny work this hard.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Fine, then. I'll be gracious and allow you the privilege of serving me.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: But let's be clear. You'd best keep the food coming and the entertainment lively. Keep this granny nice and comfortable. Otherwise... Well, I can't promise one of my little darlings won't get bored and wander off to nibble on someone.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: This granny has all the time in the world. I CAN WAIT YOU OUT.
Her threat delivered, Ayiguo hops down from the chair and turns to go. Without warning, she staggers, crumples to the floor, and curls into herself, her face twisting with pain.
Instinct moves you to reach out and help her—

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: This old body's soaked in poison, you foolish brat! Do you have a death wish?!

Ayiguo swats your hand aside. Her voice emerges hoarse. Even speech seems to cost her tremendous effort. She recovers on the floor for several minutes, then forces herself upright and staggers out of the interrogation room, leaving you alone to process what has just happened.
Ayiguo unsettles you more deeply than other Sinners. It is not merely her uncanny command over vermin and serpents; it is the warp of her logic at the root.

What others fear and loathe, she names her little darlings with genuine affection. An invasive breach, in her mind, is merely dropping by. She claims she wants the shackles to mend her body, to live as an ordinary girl, and yet that ordinary wish sounds anything but ordinary on her tongue.
You look down at the two documents resting on the desk: one a fragmented file spanning decades, the other a medical report riddled with unknowns...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Nightingale, send Ayiguo's medical report to Banyan Medical College. I need their assistance.
